title: A Thousand Mountains | A Summer in the Wind
subtitle: I liked the original melody—it felt so fresh—so I wrote new lyrics.
body:
The wind blows through your hair The tips curl lightly, brushing my heartstrings Milk tea crouches silently downstairs at your place A cool exterior, sweating a little, saying nothing
The cat and I guess which of us likes your head pats more Orange soda and cicada songs, all tucked into my trouser pockets Whose lost puppy is this, crouching beside the grass? My soaked T-shirt seems to tease this deliberate chance encounter The movie tickets and my voice both tremble a little You are beside me, yet I am like a puppet Brow furrowed, rehearsing excuses over and over How can I hold your hand?
A summer of sage Sea salt brushed by the wind You rising onto tiptoe All of them scenes from a dream
The wind blows through your hair The tips curl lightly, brushing my heartstrings A postcard cannot hold all my longing Could the puppy scrawled on the envelope and I exchange souls?
Diogenes’ little lamb Avoids the flock and the sunlight The squirrel at Eugénie’s house Loves apples, not pinecones Fibonacci’s gray rabbit Has not yet learned arithmetic The puppy who knows no romance Watches forty-two sunsets with you[1]
The wind blows through your hair The tips curl lightly, brushing my left shoulder Your warm breath tastes of strawberries Held still in this moment, the soul is light
A summer of sage Sea salt brushed by the wind You rising onto tiptoe Perhaps these are not scenes from a dream
--- [1] The repeated sunsets recall [*The Little Prince*](https://www.b612.cn/read/06.html). The number forty-two is retained from the author’s poem. The names and animals in the preceding lines are retained without assigning them additional meanings.
